title: Bitly Pricing 2026: Free Plan Limits, Paid Plans and Costs
summary: Bitly pricing ranges from free to $199 monthly, offering URL shortening, QR code generation and click tracking features depending on your plan level.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Is Bitly free to use? Yes, Bitly has a free plan, but it meters monthly short links and QR codes, so "free" lasts only until you hit those caps.


Its default short domain is shared, and analytics depth is limited. Check the current caps on Bitly's pricing page, because they have changed before.


Does Bitly charge extra for custom domains? You'll find custom domains behind paid tiers rather than on the free plan, and the number of domains included varies by tier.


Whether a second or third domain costs extra, and how much, is something we couldn't verify. Count the domains you need before comparing plans, since that count can move you up a tier.


### Do Bitly links stop working if I cancel?


After a downgrade, short links created on the shared default domain generally keep redirecting, according to Bitly's help documentation, though we haven't tested this ourselves.


The risk is with branded links. If your custom domain is tied to a paid plan, those links may stop resolving when the plan ends.


Export your link list and check the domain terms before you cancel. **Printed QR codes pointing at a branded domain** are the costliest thing to break.


### Is there a discount for nonprofits or annual billing?


Bitly has offered annual billing at a lower effective monthly rate, and it has run nonprofit programs, but we couldn't confirm current terms for either. Treat both as unverified.


Compare the annual total against twelve months of monthly billing in your own checkout, and ask Bitly sales directly about nonprofit eligibility. Annual billing also locks you in, so it only saves money if your link and QR volume is stable.


### Can I use Bitly's API on the free plan?


On free accounts, Bitly has offered API access, with rate limits and fewer features than paid tiers.


The metered unit is API requests, and the limits decide whether automated link creation is practical for you. We couldn't verify which endpoints are restricted on the free plan today.


If your workflow creates links in bulk, test it against the free plan's limits before you commit to a paid one.
